name: Citicoline (CDP-choline)
lead: Citicoline, or cytidine 5'-diphosphocholine (CDP-choline), is a nucleotide that occurs naturally in the body as an intermediate in the synthesis of phosphatidylcholine, a membrane phospholipid [1][9]. It is sold as a prescription drug in some countries for stroke and cognitive disorders and as a dietary supplement in others, including the United States, according to Grokipedia [1].

It is marketed as a cholinergic nootropic. Large randomised trials in acute ischaemic stroke and traumatic brain injury, notably ICTUS and COBRIT, did not show the benefit seen in earlier smaller studies, while pooled analyses of earlier trials had suggested a benefit [2][5][6].
No published trial has tested citicoline for any appearance outcome, and the sources reviewed contain no looksmaxxing community discussion of it.
infobox: Stroke and cognitive disorders in some countries, per Grokipedia [1]
Dietary supplement; no FDA approval as a drug for these indications, per Grokipedia [1]

paras: A 1995 review described the metabolism and actions of CDP-choline as an endogenous compound and when given exogenously [9]. Grokipedia states that after oral use it is hydrolysed, releasing choline and cytidine that cross the blood-brain barrier and are used to make phosphatidylcholine [1].

Grokipedia reports approval for acute ischaemic stroke in Japan and several European countries but not as a US prescription drug [1]. Citicoline has been studied in ischaemic stroke, traumatic brain injury, vascular cognitive impairment, optic neuropathies and glaucoma, and substance dependence [2][4][5][6][7][8][10][11][12].

In stroke, a diffusion-weighted MRI study of the effect on ischaemic lesion growth was published in 2000 [4]. A phase III randomised trial of a high oral dose in acute ischaemic stroke was published in 2001 [7], and a 2002 individual-patient pooling analysis of oral citicoline trials reported on recovery [5]. The international ICTUS trial, published in 2012 in The Lancet, sought to confirm efficacy in moderate-to-severe stroke in a larger sample and did not find an overall benefit [2].

In traumatic brain injury, the COBRIT trial of 1,213 patients published in JAMA in 2012 found no improvement in functional and cognitive status [6][13]. A pharmacotherapy review for vascular cognitive impairment also addressed citicoline [8]. Registered trials have studied citicoline in non-arteritic ischaemic optic neuropathy, visual pathway function, methamphetamine dependence and alcohol dependence, and a recruiting trial is testing it after delirium [10][11][12][14][15]. No studies were found testing citicoline for appearance outcomes.
Grokipedia describes citicoline as widely sold as a nootropic supplement in the US and EU [1]. The sources reviewed contain no discussion of it in looksmaxxing forums.

timeline.event: Introduced as a prescription drug in Europe and Japan, per Grokipedia [1].
ICTUS (stroke) and COBRIT (traumatic brain injury) trials published [2][6].

card.summary: A choline-donor nootropic studied for stroke and brain injury; no trial tests it for appearance.
card.note: Large stroke and brain-injury trials did not show overall benefit.

quick.overview:
Citicoline is a naturally occurring nucleotide that supplies choline and cytidine for membrane synthesis. It is sold as a supplement in the US and used as a drug in some countries for stroke and cognitive decline.

No trial has tested it for appearance, and it is not discussed in the looksmaxxing sources reviewed.
quick.mechanism: After ingestion it is broken down into choline and cytidine, which the brain uses to make phosphatidylcholine, a membrane phospholipid.
quick.risks: Grokipedia describes a good safety profile at therapeutic amounts. The large ICTUS and COBRIT trials did not show benefit in stroke or brain injury.
